title: 4.1 Interpreting a Derivative

icans: I can find velocity and acceleration from a position function.
I can decide when an object is at rest and whether it is speeding up or slowing down.
I can interpret a derivative as a rate of change in an application.

vocab: v(t) = s′(t), the rate of change of ___________
a(t) = v′(t), the rate of change of ___________
C′(x), the ______________ cost of producing one more item

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Velocity and acceleration: v(t) = s′(t) and a(t) = _______________.

blocks.stem: s(t) = t³ − 9t² + 24t (meters, seconds). Find v(t), a(t), v(1), and a(1).

notes: At rest: the object is at rest when v(t) = _______________.

blocks.stem: For s(t) = t³ − 9t² + 24t, when is the object at rest?

notes: Speeding up or slowing down: speeding up when v and a have the _______________ sign; slowing down when the signs are opposite.

blocks.stem: For s(t) = t³ − 9t² + 24t, is the object speeding up or slowing down at t = 1? At t = 5?

notes: Rates of change: the derivative dy/dx is the rate of change of y with respect to _______________.

blocks.stem: Find the rate of change of the area of a circle with respect to its radius when r = 5 cm.
C(x) = 0.02x² + 10x + 500 dollars. Find and interpret C′(100).
